q28.

The `Server.Start` method (`server/server.go:101-132`) calls `s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)`, which is the only place the server launches background workers.

- s3 presign runner — a plain `time.Ticker` firing every 12 hours (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12` in `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`). It's instantiated and started in `server.go:startBackgroundRunners` (`server/server.go:153-174`): an immediate `s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)` is run once synchronously at startup, then `s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)` is launched in a goroutine, which loops on the ticker until its context is cancelled during shutdown (`server/server.go:176-182`, `stopBackgroundRunners`).

That is the only background runner the server starts — no other goroutine loop exists in `server.go` or `cmd/memos/main.go` (the other `go func()` there just waits on the OS signal channel to trigger `Shutdown`, it's not a recurring job, see `cmd/memos/main.go:99-103`).

Unused scheduling infrastructure:
- `internal/scheduler` — a full cron-style scheduler package (`internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`, `job.go`, `parser.go`, `middleware.go`, described in `internal/scheduler/doc.go:1-35` as a "GitHub Actions-inspired cron job scheduler" supporting cron expressions, timezones, and middleware). It is never imported or instantiated anywhere outside its own package's tests/examples (`scheduler_test.go`, `example_test.go`, `integration_test.go`) — no call to `scheduler.New(...)` exists in `server/`, `cmd/`, or anywhere else in the codebase.
- `server/runner/memopayload.Runner` — a batch runner (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:14-24`, `RunOnce`) intended to rebuild payloads for all memos in batches. `memopayload.NewRunner` is never called anywhere in the codebase; only the plain helper function `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` is invoked synchronously (not as a background/scheduled job) from `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` and `:447` during memo create/update request handling.
